The area of $ABCD$ is $7{\text{ mm}}^{2}.$   Then, the area of $△BCD$, rounded to the **nearest integer**, is{{field-1}}${\text{ mm}}^{2}.$
worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $△ABD.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 28\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =9.899… \\  & ≈10{\text{ m}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the **nearest integer**.

The difference of the areas of $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△BCD} & ={A}_{△ABD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =10-7 \\  & =3{\text{ mm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
